answer: At dawn, every agent in the grove of the network must solve a fresh, epoch-seeded delay puzzle before its votes count. The puzzle is a verifiable delay function: it takes a fixed wall-clock time on any hardware, so a Sybil farmer spawning a thousand fake identities cannot parallelize the work. Each identity costs the same ten minutes of sequential computation, and the horizon of the epoch is too short to finish them all. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay per identity, every epoch, forever.
